# The Hunter's Moon and the God Who Provides

## Scripture
*"Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?"* — Matthew 6:26

## Reflection
October's full moon rises fat and golden this week—what our ancestors called the Hunter's Moon. After the harvest was gathered, farmers would glean their fields by its generous light, and hunters would move through the stubble, knowing winter's hunger was coming. It was a moon of provision, a lantern hung in the sky for the season of waiting.

There's something deeply comforting in how the heavens anticipate our needs. The Hunter's Moon doesn't wait until the fields are bare to shine; it rises while there's still grain to gather. It arrives like a quiet promise that the One who set it in motion has already seen the frost that's coming.

Jesus pointed His followers to the same truth, only closer to home. Look at the birds, He said. They don't plan their harvests or hoard their stores, yet they are never forgotten. The God who times the moon's fullness to the season's need also knows the exact shape of your need today. Perhaps you're in a season where the fields feel empty and the winter feels near. Take heart. The same sky that has marked your seasons with unfailing precision is held by hands that have never once dropped what they were carrying.

The Hunter's Moon reminds us: provision comes before the need is desperate. Our Father sees the frost while there's still grain to gather.

## Prayer

Father, thank You for the faithful rhythm of the moon, marking seasons we could never track alone. When fear whispers that winter will come before help arrives, remind us of Your provision—the birds fed, the harvest gathered, the moon rising right on time. You have never forgotten us. Help us trust You with what's coming, resting in the care that has never failed. In Jesus' name, Amen.
